qt: to the Commission Stanisław Tyszka (ESN) Subject:

For years, the Commission restricted Poland’s access to EU funds, invoking the rule of law and judicial independence. Today, as Donald Tusk’s team unlawfully seizes control of the Constitutional Tribunal, the Commission’s position gives his government political cover. Hiding behind the Sejm’s right to elect judges, the Commission is legitimising the unlawful actions of Tusk’s team by turning a blind eye to the strong-arm and legally baseless manner in which the leadership of the Constitutional Tribunal was taken over. The party politicisation of the Constitutional Tribunal by PiS does not give Tusk and his team the right to violate the Constitution and the law. The rule of law cannot mean punishing inconvenient governments while indulging political allies. Poland is a sovereign state and the Commission is not a European super-government entitled to adjudicate on internal constitutional disputes. Its role as guardian of the Treaties does not entitle it to overstep their bounds or to back the unlawful actions of governments that are politically friendly towards it. 1.

Why is the Commission siding with Tusk’s team in the dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal, applying double standards on the rule of law and thereby interfering in the constitutional affairs of Poland as a sovereign state?

Did the Polish government or its representatives give the Commission advance notice of the planned ousting of the President and Vice-President of the Constitutional Tribunal and the takeover of the Tribunal’s leadership? Did they consult the Commission on these actions or agree with it on how they were to be carried out? If so, when did such contacts take place, who took part in them and what position did the Commission take?
